title: Slip Coding.pdf — page 14
text:
Financial Terms Review
14
Term Simple Meaning Real Property Insurance Example (CAT Modeling Context)
Blanket Limit One single limit for all locations combined under a policy.
A policy covers 10 locations across Florida with a Blanket Limit of USD 100M. 
If any location is hit by a hurricane, losses from all sites together cannot 
exceed USD 100M.
Part Of Shows how much of a larger insurance layer the specific policy 
covers.
Layer is USD 50M xs 50M. The insured buys USD 20M Part Of 50M. CAT 
modeler applies only USD 20M limit from the 50M layer.
Excess of (Attachment Point) Losses are paid only above this threshold. Policy: USD 100M xs 25M. For hurricane loss of USD 40M, insurer pays 40 – 
25 = 15M.
Blanket Deductible One deductible applied to the entire policy (not per location).
A global retail chain (50 stores) has Blanket Deductible = USD 5M. If multiple 
stores are damaged in a cyclone, all losses combined share one USD 5M 
deductible.
Minimum / Maximum 
Deductible Policy Deductible cap when deductible is percent-based. Policy has 5% of TIV per location, but min = USD 250k, max = USD 2M. If TIV is 
low , at least 250k applies. For high TIV sites, max 2M applies.
Coverage Value Sum insured for Building, Contents, BI. Location in Texas: Building = 20M, Contents = 5M, BI = 3M. These values go 
into RMS/AIR exposure inputs.
Coverage Limit / Coverage 
Deductible Limit or deductible that applies separately to each coverage. BI sub-limit: USD 10M BI limit, even though Building/Contents are covered 
higher. During CAT modeling, BI loss is capped at 10M.
Site Limit / Site Deductible Limit or deductible that applies to an individual location. Japan factory has Site Limit = JPY 2B even though blanket limit for policy is 
higher. Location-specific deductible: JPY 50M per site for earthquake.
